question: According to complaints from citizens and petitions and complaints lodged by users of the Egnatia Odos with the Hellenic Competition Commission, after the motorway was taken over by a private concessionaire a series of tunnels along the Igoumenitsa-Panagia section were simultaneously reduced to a single lane back in 2026 and have remained so ever since.

This section, which is approximately 123 kilometres long, has numerous long twin tunnels spanning more than 33 kilometres in total. The single lane system applies to the entire length of the tunnels as well as to sections before them, involving traffic and vehicle speed restrictions.

Meanwhile, motorway users continue to be charged full toll fees, raising questions about whether the price is proportional to the service provided and about whether this practice complies with EU law. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Is the extensive and simultaneous reduction of motorway tunnels to single lane traffic for the purposes of performing checks and improving safety compatible with the European tunnel safety framework and the law on trans-European transport?
Has it examined or does it intend to examine whether these measures affect road safety or compliance with European requirements for the operation of road infrastructure?

Is the continued collection of full toll fees compatible with EU competition law and the principle of proportionality when there are significant traffic restrictions resulting from technical measures or interventions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.7.2026) 1. Directive 2004/54/EC on minimum safety requirements for tunnels in the Trans-European Road Network1 does not prevent the reduction of the number of lanes on motorways in tunnels to a single lane, if the safety requirements are met.

Similarly, neither Regulation (EU) 2024/1679 on Union guidelines for the development of the trans-European transport network2, nor Directive 2008/96/EC on road infrastructure safety management3, forbid the reduction to one of the number of lanes of a road. 2. The Commission did not assess and does not plan to challenge these measures which have been put in place to check and improve the safety along the motorway.

Traffic organisation measures fall within the remit of the national competent authorities. 3. Directive 1999/62/EC on the charging of vehicles for the use of road infrastructures4 requires that the level of the infrastructure charge element of a toll levied upon heavy-duty vehicles is equal to, or less than, the level necessary to recover the cost of the infrastructure.
There are no specific conditions in competition law on the level of the toll fees in relation to traffic restrictions.

1 OJ L 167, 30.4.2004, p. 39, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2004/54/oj. 2 OJ L 2024/1679, 28.6.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1679/oj. 3 OJ L 319 29.11.2008, p. 59, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2008/96/oj. 4 OJ L 187 20.7.1999, p. 42, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/1999/62/oj.
